blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Financial analysis at the executive level supports the decisions that matter most — acquisitions, divestments, major investments, pricing strategies, market entries. The stakes are bigger, but the discipline is the same: tell the story, recommend the action, and name the one assumption that would change the conclusion if it turned out to be wrong.

At this level, what separates excellent analysis from average is the willingness to identify the assumption you are most nervous about, and to show the decision under that scenario. It is uncomfortable work. Senior leaders would usually prefer a clean recommendation. But the leaders who demand the uncomfortable version are the ones who rarely get surprised by the outcome.

Were we to present only the central case, we would be hiding the one number that matters most — the sensitivity to the assumption we were least confident about. Good analysis does not hide. It invites the executive team into the uncomfortable question, early, when there is still time to change the decision.

items.q: According to the text, the discipline behind an executive financial recommendation involves…
options: telling the story, recommending the action, and naming the decisive assumption
avoiding any assumption that cannot be proven
deferring to the preferences of senior leaders
presenting the most optimistic forecast available
items.why: "tell the story, recommend the action, and name the one assumption that would change the conclusion".

items.q: What does the text say distinguishes excellent analysis from average analysis?
options: The seniority of the audience
The volume of data presented
The willingness to expose the assumption you are most nervous about
The precision of the central case
items.why: "what separates excellent analysis from average is the willingness to identify the assumption you are most nervous about".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A clean, single recommendation is the most responsible thing to deliver.
Sensitivity to a shaky assumption can be the most important number.
Good analysis surfaces discomfort rather than concealing it.
Executives benefit from seeing the scenario in which the weakest assumption fails.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta contra a recomendação 'limpa' que esconde a sensibilidade — logo o autor discordaria dela.

items.q: The phrase "the ones who rarely get surprised by the outcome" suggests that…
options: confronting uncomfortable scenarios in advance reduces nasty surprises later
surprises are unavoidable at the executive level
outcomes are impossible to predict
leaders prefer not to know the downside
items.why: Inferência: quem exige a versão desconfortável já viu o cenário ruim, então raramente é pego de surpresa.

items.q: Why does the text stress inviting the executive team into the uncomfortable question "early"?
options: Because there is still time to change the decision at that point
Because early meetings are easier to schedule
Because the analyst wants to avoid blame
Because the central case is only ready early on
items.why: "early, when there is still time to change the decision" — cedo, o desfecho ainda pode ser alterado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando o caso da aquisição ao comitê. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. I want to walk you through this acquisition in two versions, and I would ask you to sit with the second one for a moment, because it is the one that keeps me awake.

The central case is straightforward. On our base assumptions, the deal creates value from year two, and the returns comfortably clear our hurdle rate. If nothing else changed, I would recommend we proceed without hesitation.

But there is one assumption I am genuinely nervous about — the pace at which we retain the target's largest customers after close. Everything hinges on it. Were that retention rate to fall ten points below plan, the picture inverts: the deal destroys value for the first four years, and we would be relying on a recovery we cannot yet promise.

So my recommendation is deliberately uncomfortable. I am not asking you to bless the central case and move on. I am asking you to decide whether we can live with the second scenario — because if we cannot, the time to walk away is now, not eighteen months from now with the money already spent.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: In the central case, when does James say the deal starts creating value?
options: Immediately after close
Not within the forecast period
From year two
Only after four years
items.why: "the deal creates value from year two, and the returns comfortably clear our hurdle rate."

items.q: Which assumption is James most nervous about?
options: The pace of retaining the target's largest customers after close
The timing of regulatory approval
The accuracy of the target's accounts
The cost of financing the deal
items.why: "the pace at which we retain the target's largest customers after close… Everything hinges on it."

items.q: What happens to the case if retention falls ten points below plan?
options: The deal must be renegotiated at a lower price
The picture inverts and the deal destroys value for the first four years
The deal still clears the hurdle rate, just later
The returns are unaffected
items.why: "Were that retention rate to fall ten points below plan, the picture inverts: the deal destroys value for the first four years."

items.q: What does James mean when he says his recommendation is "deliberately uncomfortable"?
options: He wants the committee to reject the deal
He is unsure whether the deal is legal
He dislikes presenting to the committee
He is forcing the committee to confront the downside scenario rather than just approve the base case
items.why: Inferência: ele não pede o carimbo no caso central; pede que decidam se aguentam o cenário ruim.

items.q: Why does James stress deciding "now, not eighteen months from now"?
options: Because walking away is cheap now but costly once the money is committed
Because the retention data expires quickly
Because the target may withdraw the offer
Because the committee meets only once a year
items.why: Inferência: 'with the money already spent' — depois de gastar, sair é caro; agora ainda dá para desistir.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board approved the acquisition of the smaller trader." An acquisition is…
options: a joint marketing agreement
a change to the pricing model
the sale of a business unit
the purchase of another company or business
items.why: Acquisition = aquisição: comprar outra empresa ou negócio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "To free up capital, the group announced the ___ of its loss-making Asian operations."
options: sensitivity
market entry
divestment
assumption
items.why: Divestment = desinvestimento: vender/desfazer-se de uma operação.

items.q: "The whole recommendation rests on one shaky assumption." An assumption is…
options: a final decision
something taken to be true without proof
a confirmed fact
a legal obligation
items.why: Assumption = premissa: algo que se toma como verdadeiro sem prova definitiva.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The model shows high ___ to the retention rate — a small change there swings the answer."
options: market entry
sensitivity
acquisition
divestment
items.why: Sensitivity = sensibilidade: quanto o resultado muda quando a premissa muda.

items.q: "With so much capital committed, the stakes could hardly be higher." Here stakes means…
options: the legal paperwork required
the number of people in the room
what stands to be won or lost
the deadlines involved
items.why: Stakes = o que está em jogo, aquilo que se pode ganhar ou perder.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em comitês de investimento e decisões estratégicas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The investment committee still has to sign off on the acquisition." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
delay indefinitely
comment informally
circulate for review
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the retention assumption." They…
options: approved it at once
postponed reading it
resisted or challenged it
rewrote the whole model
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "If the downside case is right, tweaking the price won't move the needle." This means it will…
options: cost more than expected
take too long to measure
provoke resistance from the board
not make a meaningful difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Before we commit the capital, let's stress-test the weakest assumption." To stress-test means to…
options: delegate it to the audit team
remove it from the model
present it in the best possible light
check how it holds up under harsh conditions
items.why: Stress-test = submeter a cenários extremos para ver se a premissa aguenta.

items.q: "If we cannot live with the downside, we should walk away from the deal." To walk away means to…
options: postpone the vote
abandon or decline the deal
accept it with conditions
renegotiate the terms
items.why: Walk away = desistir do negócio, abandonar a mesa.
